Calibrate FINN on revisited plots

Source: R/calibrer_finn.R
calibrer_finn.Rd

Fits the mechanistic processes of FINN (Forest Informed Neural Networks, Kaber et al.; growth, mortality, regeneration, competition) on plots measured twice, so that the model can then simulate stand trajectories (spec 068, chantier D, step 3). One FINN site is one plot, one FINN step is the interval between the two visits.

Usage

calibrer_finn(
  arbres,
  environnement,
  processus = "mecaniste",
  surface_placette = 0.7,
  epoques = 600L,
  taux_apprentissage = 0.003,
  part_essences = 0.9,
  min_arbres_essence = 300L,
  pas_annees = 5,
  graine = 42L,
  dossier = NULL
)

Arguments

arbres

data.frame, one row per tree and pair of visits, with columns:

placette

plot identifier.

essence

species code (character).

d1, d2

diameter at breast height (cm) at the first and second visit; d1 is NA for recruits, d2 for dead or cut trees.

poids

stems per hectare represented by the tree (the IFN W): the weight of the first visit for a tree followed, the theoretical weight of its circle for a recruit.

statut

"vivant" (alive at both visits), "mort" (died or left the stand), "coupe" (cut) or "recrute" (new at the second visit).

Cut trees are removed from the initial state: the cut is assumed to happen at the start of the interval, so that FINN learns the natural dynamics only (interventions are applied between steps, D-2).

environnement

data.frame, one row per plot: placette and the numeric environmental variables (e.g. summer maximum temperature, annual rainfall, soil depth), in natural units (FINN standardises them). Plots with a missing value are dropped.

processus

Character. "mecaniste" (default) is the only value for now: neural components come only once a cross-validation shows a gain on revisited plots (D-3).

surface_placette

Numeric. Area of the FINN patch, in hectares. Default 0.7. FINN rounds cohort sizes to integers: with the 15 m circle of the IFN (0.0707 ha) a tree of the 6 m circle counts 6.25 stems rounded to 6, which adds noise of 1.4 m2/ha (SD) on the initial basal area and a bias on recruitment; at 0.7 ha both vanish (spec 068, section 9).

epoques

Integer. Number of training epochs. Default 600.

taux_apprentissage

Numeric. Learning rate. Default 0.003 (better held-out error than 0.01 on BFC, spec 068).

part_essences

Numeric in (0, 1]. Species kept by decreasing initial basal area until they cover this share; the others are pooled in "other". Default 0.9.

min_arbres_essence

Integer. Minimum number of initial trees (alive or dead at the first visit) for a species to get its own parameters; below it the species goes to "other", even within part_essences. Default 300: on BFC, species with 130 to 140 trees gave unstable parameters (predictions of several hundred m2/ha on a few plots in two bootstrap calibrations out of four, spec 068).

pas_annees

Numeric. Years between the two visits, kept as metadata for the simulations. Default 5.

graine

Integer. Random seed (R and torch). Default 42.

dossier

Character or NULL. Folder where FINN writes checkpoints every 100 epochs. Default NULL (none).

Value

A list of class "finn_calibration": modele (the fitted FINN model, a torch object: save it with torch::torch_save(), not saveRDS()), essences, variables_env, surface_placette, pas_annees, recruits_dbh, n_placettes, epoques, taux_apprentissage, processus, placettes (identifiers of the calibration plots, checked by conformer_finn()).

Details

Requires the suggested packages FINN, torch (with libtorch, torch::install_torch()) and data.table; the function stops with a clear message when they are missing.

On 1000 IFN plots of Bourgogne-Franche-Comte revisited after 5 years, with summer maximum temperature, annual rainfall (E-OBS) and soil depth, the error on the basal area at 5 years of 1000 other plots was 3.36 m2/ha (bias +0.37, 40 minutes of CPU), against 3.58 for a linear regression and 4.24 for persistence (data-raw/prototype_finn_calibration.R).

References

Kaber Y., Hartig F. et al. FINN: Forest Informed Neural Networks. R package version 0.1.0, CRAN.
